items.label: text
items.text: The 1– ions formed by the halogens (Group 7) are collectively called halide ions. Chloride, bromide and iodide ions are all halide ions.

items.label: text
items.text: The acid is added to react with and remove other anions which might also produce precipitates with silver nitrate solution, for example carbonate and hydroxide ions. You must not use hydrochloric acid (or hydrobromic acid or hydroiodic acid) as you will be adding halide ions and you are certain to obtain a precipitate.

items.text: 1 Name the gas being described in each of the following cases.

items.text: a A green gas that bleaches damp litmus paper.

items.text: b A gas that dissolves readily in water to produce a solution with a pH of about 11.

items.text: c A gas that produces a white precipitate with limewater.

items.text: d A gas that pops when a lighted splint is placed in it.

items.text: 3A is an orange solid, which dissolves in water to give an orange solution. When sodium hydroxide solution is added to a solution of A, an orangebrown precipitate, B, is formed. Adding dilute nitric acid and silver nitrate solution to a solution of A gives a white precipitate, C.
